items.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: I play Lady Day’s pianist, Jimmy Powers.

ctx.x: I have two projects. I did a “Live at the Blue Note” which I’m very proud of. And I finally did a Henry Mancini tune, I talked about earlier on. I had never done Henry Mancini in my book. So I did “Dreamsville” from Peter Gunn. And did more piano. Because I was always behind the scenes, getting the saxophone player up there, the trumpet player, but now I’m doing the front line. I have a studio project I did on my own with some great people on it, that I’m trying to bring out independently. I’m working on a…

high schools, colleges, to talk about the relationship between the pianist and the vocalist, on all different kinds of levels. And the preparation needed from both. I’ve done some acting. I acted in a play, a professional production of a play called “Lady Day at Emerson’s Bar & Grill,” and I play Lady Day’s pianist, Jimmy Powers. I had a few lines, but it was still a whole new kind of experience. So that’s something I may even check out a little more. And I’d like to do some more scoring. I did a film for Danny…
